results.proposal_summary: The Nature for Health (N4H) Phase II Expression of Interest, funded by Germany (BMUV/IKI) through an initial €50 million contribution to the N4H Multi-Partner Trust Fund, invited governments of ODA-eligible countries and regional intergovernmental entities to apply for up to USD 2,250,000 in seed funding per proposal to implement integrated, preventative One Health approaches addressing the nature-health interface, including upstream prevention of zoonotic spillover and biodiversity-health integration. Eligible applicants were national or sub-national governments and regional intergovernmental entities from countries on the OECD DAC ODA Recipients list, excluding those that participated in Phase I. The application window was open from 10 January 2025 to 7 April 2025, with selection announced in August 2025. Non-governmental entities were explicitly ineligible. No co-financing was generally required, though co-funding was needed for activities in non-ODA-eligible countries within regional proposals.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call focuses exclusively on pandemic prevention, biodiversity, and One Health approaches at the nature-health interface, with no connection to ILO mandate areas such as labour standards, employment, social protection, or decent work.

The call provides non-reimbursable financial support (monthly stipends) to eligible students enrolled in DigiQ-affiliated Master's programmes or recent DigiQ graduates from EU member states and DEP associated countries, enabling exchange semesters or thesis projects at partner DigiQ institutions. results.proposal_summary: The European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN), with European Union support under the DIGITAL 2021–2027 programme, has launched a temporary rolling call for protection grants aimed at fact-checking organisations facing harassment, legal threats, physical danger, or cybersecurity incidents. The total budget is €80,000, with individual grants of up to €20,000 (exceptionally €40,000) on a 50% co-financing basis. Eligible applicants are for-profit or non-profit legal entities that are EFCSN-certified fact-checkers or organisations demonstrating intent to comply with the European Code of Standards, located in the EU or DEP-associated countries; single applicants only (no consortia). With a total budget of up to £20 million over approximately 2.5 years (August 2026 to March 2029), the programme aims to transition Uganda's refugee response from a predominantly humanitarian model toward self-reliance and resilience for refugees and host communities. It focuses on two pillars: (1) meeting core humanitarian needs (food security, protection) of the most vulnerable refugees, particularly new arrivals; and (2) enabling economically vulnerable refugee and host community households—especially women, girls, youth, and persons with disabilities—to transition away from humanitarian dependence. results.proposal_summary: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), Cairo Office, issued an Expression of Interest for communication, awareness raising, and visibility services to support the Strengthening the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPD) Project in Egypt, funded under EU contribution agreement NDICI-GEO-NEAR/2023/450-429. The EOI seeks service providers capable of delivering radio awareness series, digital/social media awareness campaigns, and communication and visibility materials. This is a service procurement process, not a grant call; the budget is indicative at this stage. The EOI submission deadline was 20 May 2026 at 11:00, which has now passed. No grant amount threshold is stated. The call is directed at service providers (companies, NGOs, or equivalent) and does not include UN agencies or international organisations as eligible applicants.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call relates to disability rights and awareness in Egypt, which has marginal overlap with ILO's work on inclusive employment and decent work, but the procurement is for media/communication services unrelated to ILO's core mandate areas.

Eligible partners include institutional ESG investors, DFIs, impact investors, sovereign wealth funds, and diaspora networks. The facility focuses on ocean innovation, sustainable tourism, marine conservation, and climate-resilient livelihoods for 15,000+ coastal community members. This is an investment mobilisation vehicle, not a traditional grant call, and no submission deadline is specified.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The facility touches on coastal community livelihoods and climate resilience, which have tangential relevance to ILO decent work and just transitions mandates, but its primary purpose is private capital mobilisation through blue bonds — not technical assistance or labour standards work.

results.proposal_summary: The ASSIST Facility 2.0, hosted under the Joint SDG Fund, is a $150M blended finance investment vehicle for Indonesia seeking to catalyse an additional $10 billion in sustainable impact financing by 2030. The facility targets sovereign wealth funds, DFIs, Islamic finance institutions, and institutional ESG investors — not implementing organisations — offering 6-8% financial returns with 10:1 to 15:1 leverage multipliers through thematic bond issuance (sovereign blue bonds, municipal sukuk) and venture capital deployment. There is no submission deadline or open application window; interested investors are invited to contact the Joint SDG Fund secretariat directly. The ILO is not an eligible participant, as this is a private capital mobilisation vehicle, not a grant programme for technical assistance.
